name: raw-posterior-ensembles
title: Raw-feature transfer from ensembles of pretrained networks
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: Simultaneous nearby-parity transfer from independent raw posterior banks; an antithetic reflected pair gives a separate one-trained-bank construction with no comparator-norm increase.
qualification: Paired source data and cold finite-width energy hypotheses. Independent banks and deliberately coupled reflected banks are distinct protocols. Exact posterior pretraining is assumed; the deterministic implication also applies to optimization attaining the stated bounds.

name: quantitative-condensate-count
title: Polynomial probabilities of extra exceptional neurons
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: Sharp fixed-count ReLU posterior hierarchy: each extra macroscopic neuron costs width to the power minus (r-3)/2. A count-and-rank formula identifies the additional cost of new output directions.
qualification: Full-cube source labels, fixed even dimension at least six, fixed sufficiently small norm cutoff. Conventional asymptotic probability proof, not an online mistake theorem.

name: metropolis-corrected-posterior
title: Finite Metropolis corrections for a condensed ReLU posterior
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: A general independence-Metropolis perturbation hierarchy and sharp neural sampling errors: each fixed correction adds a half-power of width until the omitted-sector floor.
qualification: Square or logistic full-cube likelihood, fixed even dimension at least six. Expected linear width cost has unrestricted dimension constants and assumes exact real arithmetic. This is a proposal-started correction theorem, not arbitrary-start mixing.

name: exact-hard-sector-sampler
title: Exact sector sampling for condensed ReLU posteriors
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: Exact ReLU posterior draws conditional on a specified finite union of count sectors. Including finitely many extra-neuron sectors gives any fixed polynomial total-variation accuracy at expected linear width cost.
qualification: Hard margins and square/logistic full-cube likelihoods; fixed dimension and number of retained sectors. Constants may be enormous. Dummy critical draws cancel unknown normalizers in the multisector mixture; no practical dimension-uniform or bit-complexity bound.

name: softplus-sector-asymptotics
title: Smoothing changes the fluctuations of Bayesian neural condensates
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: Fixed-temperature softplus evidence prefactors, stretched-exponential extra-count rates, shifted Gaussian fluctuations, and a one-neuron crossover at activation inverse temperature of order square root of width.
qualification: Full-cube source labels, fixed even dimension and positive softplus temperature. Uses the preceding marked-configuration condensation theorem; does not give small-data learning or dimension-uniform sampling.

name: softplus-polynomial-sampling
title: Arbitrary polynomial accuracy for softplus posterior sampling
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: A truncated slightly supercritical proposal and pilot-independent leading error observable give a sharp quarter-power improvement per fixed Metropolis correction, including after pilot averaging.
qualification: Square or logistic full-cube likelihood, fixed dimension and activation temperature. A positive amplitude enclosure is supplied, or obtained explicitly when the target margin exceeds 3/8. Linear expected width cost is in idealized exact real arithmetic.

name: geometric-fourier-mistake-path
title: An explicit exponential mistake path in signed Fourier completion
status: A complete inductive primal-dual proof of an exponential vertex path for geometrically decaying Fourier priorities, plus obstructions for inverse-power priorities and for slowly decaying geometric priorities.
qualification: A reduced signed-mass optimization problem, not a continuous-prior conditioning theorem. Its economical neural realization remains open; the separate control-rail companion proves the observed-margin-only neural lower bound by a different construction.

name: logarithmic-smoothing-threshold
title: A logarithmic separation between local smoothing and rare neural features
group: 2. Bayesian feature learning and prior tails
status: Joint width/activation-temperature count exponents at square root of width divided by log width; singular highest-finite-moment responses; positive Fourier moment ordering and centered random-feature and initialization tangent-kernel ordering, including a strict shift of normalized variance toward higher Fourier degrees; and signed second- and third-order boundary formulas for the critical normalizer.
qualification: Fixed dimension and full-cube conditioning for the count theorem. Critical moment statements concern individual neurons. The six-dimensional covariance response is rank 38; even dimensions at least eight have a regular second-order covariance response. No full-posterior fluctuation or sampler theorem is claimed in the joint regime.

name: observed-margin-control-lower-bound
title: Superpolynomial strong-prior ReLU mistakes with margins only on observed inputs
status: A control-rail dual proves 2^(k-1) confident observed-margin-only mistakes for isotropic-Gaussian shallow ReLU learning with dimension O(k), teacher width O(k^2), and polynomial coefficients. Includes a quantitative prior scale, finite hinge regularization, a separate width-first result, and a standard-softplus extension.
qualification: Strong-prior limit at each fixed ReLU width N >= 2^(550k+342). The calibration prefix is large; these unique minimum-cost completions intrinsically require exponentially many active neurons and prior observations. A finite prior over small integer teachers has a polynomial mistake bound. Uses the shared rail norm and path ordering; conventional new proofs with selected Lean components, not a complete formalization or independent review.

name: gaussian-cosine-mistake-path
title: Maximal confident mistakes for a Gaussian cosine-network limit
status: A width-one cosine target gives 2^d-1 confident observed-margin mistakes in lexicographic order in the width-first cold limit. A finite family already gives 2^(d-1) confident mistakes at prior variance of order 1/d and width exp(O(d log(d+1))), for fixed confidence; width one has O(d^2) lifetime mistakes at that scale. A separate explicit finite family makes all but the first prediction wrong. At every fixed positive prior scale, a finite exponential width also gives an exponential tail of confident majority errors, of order (1+exp(-2 sigma^2))^d/sqrt(d), while width one has O_sigma(d log(d+1)) lifetime mistakes.
qualification: Odd dimension, cosine activation, central-limit normalization, and limit order are material. Only one initial labeled input. Exponential width is necessary for the displayed exponential sampling failures; no polynomial-width or fixed-width strong-prior lower bound. The polynomial-scale order is mean selected; the all-but-first cold order is lexicographic. Conventional proof, exact finite matrix/KKT checks, no complete Lean formalization or independent review.

name: softplus-gaussian-width-separation
title: Exponential online mistakes from widening Gaussian softplus and tanh learners
status: A standard-softplus or tanh shallow learner makes 2^(d-1) confident observed-margin-only mistakes at prior variance of order d^-3 and sufficient finite width exp(O(d log(d+1))), at fixed confidence. The parity target has a rational width-(d+1) teacher with polynomial coefficients; that narrow learner has an O(d^8) lifetime mistake bound under the same Gaussian scale.
qualification: Odd dimension at least three for softplus; even dimension at least two for tanh; central-limit normalization; deterministic Gaussian-mean-selected input order with one initial label. The inverse-parity spectrum dominates by an explicit positive-integral moment bound. This is a finite-parameter, exponential-width result, not a polynomial-width ReLU or fixed-width strong-prior theorem. Conventional proof with selected finite precision inequalities in Lean, not full formalization or independent review. At that prior scale, widths at least d+1 need N = Omega(2^d/d^3) for softplus or Omega(2^d/d^4) for tanh for an exponential majority mistake count.

name: lexicographic-degree-kernel-mistakes
title: Maximal lexicographic parity mistakes for degree-ordered kernels
status: Every positive radial Boolean-cube kernel with nonincreasing degree eigenvalues and a strict final drop makes 2^d-1 lexicographic parity mistakes under exact minimum-norm interpolation. Covers Gaussian ReLU and softplus random-feature kernels in odd dimension and tanh in even dimension, and sufficiently wide finite random-feature readout fitting. Also covers nonnegative layer-weighted ReLU/softplus initialization tangent kernels in odd dimension at least three, including both-layer and incoming-gradient-only training. A positive-power-series criterion also covers the explicitly normalized fixed ReLU NNGP and NTK recursions at every depth at least two and every dimension at least two.
qualification: Exact output observations, fixed hidden features, and minimum-norm readout fitting or fixed-kernel gradient flow run to interpolation. A compact teacher exists in the same activation class. For each fixed activation temperature, width exp(C d) log(2/zeta) suffices with probability at least 1-zeta; full-cube Gram rank also requires exponentially many scalar features. Positive-margin conditioning and hidden-feature learning are not proved by this recursion. Conventional proof, exact finite matrix checks, no full Lean formalization or independent review. The finite-Jacobian extension uses frozen Gaussian Jacobian features and a zero-output linearized model; evolving nonlinear training and uncentered initial outputs are excluded. The deep-kernel corollary fixes the input-bias normalization and does not assert a finite-deep-network width bound or nonlinear training result. The margin-activity conjecture is proved for dyadic and two-block prefix families in every dimension; the general prefix case remains open.
